model: TC300 Commercial Thermostats (TC300B-G / TC300C-G / TC320B-G / TC320C-G)
equipment_type: Thermostat (fan coil, conventional and heat pump)
applies_to: Honeywell TC300 and Wi-Fi TC320 commercial touchscreen thermostats for fan coils, conventional units and heat pumps.
summary: The TC300 family are commercial touchscreen thermostats that run fan coil, conventional or heat pump equipment. All models talk BACnet MS/TP; the TC320 models add Wi-Fi with BACnet IP. The guide lists the objects chapter by chapter: I/O configuration, sensor and output status, alarms, operating state, setpoints, network inputs, service mode and schedule.
notes: The guide has no read/write column. Access here is inferred: phy_ inputs, no_ network outputs and Alarm objects are read-only; Cfg_ and ni_ objects are writable.
Instances marked with an asterisk in the guide exist only on the TC3xxB models; they are flagged '(TC3xxB models only)' in the description.

The guide prints Cfg_CustomizeSensor1Name/2Name/3Name as Binary Value 2/3/4, which clashes with ni_ADREn (BV 2) and ni_ShutdownState (BV 4); these three name objects are left out. Cfg_SylkCalOffset_SylkBus2CO2 has no instance printed and is also left out.
Objects that appear in more than one chapter are listed once.
Which outputs and inputs are active depends on the equipment type (MV 7) and the I/O assignment objects.

integration.summary: Write the system mode to MV 3 ni_ApplicationMode and occupancy to MV 6 ni_OccupancySensorState (or schedule state MV 1), and adjust the occupied setpoints AV 7 / AV 4. Read space temperature AV 2001, effective setpoints AV 2003 / AV 2004, effective occupancy MV 2014 and the alarm objects. The BMS can feed space temperature, humidity, CO2 and outdoor air through the ni_ inputs.

minimum_points.why: System mode: auto, cool, heat, fan only, off
minimum_points.name: ni_ApplicationMode

minimum_points.why: Network occupancy: occupied, unoccupied, bypass, standby
minimum_points.name: ni_OccupancySensorState

minimum_points.why: Fan speed: auto, low, medium, high
minimum_points.name: Cfg_FanCoilManualSpeedSel

integration.enable: The thermostat runs on its own; the BMS steers it through the ni_ network inputs (application mode, occupancy, schedule state, shutdown BV 4). ni_ApplicationMode is not kept over a power cycle.
integration.heartbeat: Network fail detect: when a bound network input is not updated within its fail-detect delay (0-3600 s), it falls back to Invalid, the last good value or a fixed value. Per-input enable, fallback and delay objects exist for occupancy (BV 159, AV 262, MV 2021, AV 263), shutdown (BV 164, AV 273, BV 165, AV 274) and network sensors (BV 2087, AV 2507, AV 2508).
integration.remote_sensors: Network inputs: ni_SpaceTemp AV 104, ni_SpaceRH AV 80, ni_SpaceCO2 AV 2511, ni_OutdoorTemp AV 89, ni_OutdoorHum AV 194, ni_DATemp AV 2024 and ni_PipeTempMode MV 2012. Network sensor configuration decides whether these are used.
setup: MS/TP: the thermostat auto-detects the baud rate in the first four minutes after start-up, otherwise 76,800. Auto MAC addressing is on by default; MAC and Device ID can be set on the screen.
BACnet IP (TC320 models only) runs over Wi-Fi; Device ID, network number and UDP port are set on the BACnet IP settings page.
gotchas: Schedule and calendar objects have limits: the calendar object is not supported by the schedule object.
Service mode (BV 6 ni_ServiceModeEn) lets the network drive outputs directly; set it back to NoOverride after commissioning.
The guide says COV works for up to 20 points, but its known-issues table says COV is not supported; plan to poll.
